plan: My value is $30. In a first-price sealed bid auction with random values between $0-$49, rational strategy is complex. Other bidders also want to maximize profit. I'll bid strategically below my true value to create potential profit margin. Since values are uniformly distributed, I'll bid around the midpoint of my value - slightly below $30 to create room for potential gain if I win. Estimating other bidders might also bid strategically around their values.

In a second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$49, a dominant strategy is typically to bid close to, but not exceeding, my true value. My value is $7. Other rational bidders will likely do similar. I expect average bids around their private values. Since my value is relatively low, I'll bid slightly above my value to have a chance of winning, but not so high that I risk negative earnings. A bid around $8-$9 seems strategic.

In a single-round second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. Since my private value is $36, I'll bid strategically. Other rational bidders will likely bid near their own values. I'll bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer - this protects against overpaying if their values are high. A bid around $34-$35 seems optimal, balancing potential win probability with profit protection.
